Madison All-City Swim & Dive League — 1980-1989 Swim PDF Text Extracts
==============================================================================

Raw text extracted from the swim-related PDFs published on the league
history archive at https://allcityswimdive.org/league-history/1980s/,
covering the Swim Results, Swim Heat Sheets, and Swim News documents for
1980-1989. This is raw extracted text only -- no parsing of names, ages,
teams, or times into structured fields. Text is extracted page by page in
original page order. Native extraction (pdftotext -layout) was tried first;
where that returned empty or garbled output, the PDF was OCR'd with
ocrmypdf --force-ocr (Tesseract) and the OCR sidecar text is used instead.
OCR output may contain the usual OCR artifacts (misread characters,
garbled spacing) since these are old mimeographed/typewritten sheets.

Note: 1983 had no Swim Results/Heat Sheets/News PDFs published on the
league history site (only Dive Results); 1984 had only a Swim News PDF
(no Swim Results or Heat Sheets PDF published). Heat Sheets PDFs were
only published for 1980 and 1985 in this decade.

==============================================================================

File: 1980_Swim_HeatSheets.pdf
Source PDF: https://allcityswimdive.org/history/1980/1980_Swim_HeatSheets.pdf
Extraction method: OCR (ocrmypdf --force-ocr, Tesseract) — native extraction was empty/garbled.

West Side
Swim Club

July 31- Aug. 1 & 2, 1980
WELCOME TO WEST SIDE!

‘The West Side Swim Club is pleased to welcome all swimmers,

coaches, parents, and spectators to the 1980 All City Pool Meet.
Many people throughout the city have pointed toward this event
ag the culmination of the summer swimming season. It represents
an opportunity for the participants to demonstrate their level of
individual and team achievement in an atmosphere of friendly com-
petition. | :

In this spirit, we extend best wishes to all the competitors.
We also want to thank the many staff and volunteer workers who
have assisted in putting this meet together.

We are delighted to have you join us for this event.

       NL owners to consider Kuhn's fate
          NEW YORK ( A P ) — Storm clouds gathered over Commissioner
       Bowie Kuhn Thursday after National League owners called a special
       meeting to consider his re-election.
          Kuhn's status is among the topics to be discussed Aug. 18-19 in San
       Diego at baseball's regular summer meetings, but the NL will con-
      vene a day earlier to consider the commissioner's situation.
          The special meeting was requested by the New York Mets, St.
      Louis Cardinals and Houston Astros, all reported to be against Kuhn's
      re-election to a third term. If those teams get a fourth league club to
      join them, they could force Kuhn's resignation or firing.
          Kuhn's contract expires in August 1983, but under terms of his con-
      tract the commissioner must be advised by the owners between six to
      15 months before that date whether they plan to rehire him.

    Big Ten opposes USFL draft plans
       CHICAGO (AP) — Big Ten Conference football coaches approved
   Friday a resolution that would ban United States Football League
   coaches and scouts from conference campuses if the new profes-
   sional league conducts a December draft.
       In response, USFL Commissioner Chet Simmons said college
   players drafted by the USFL before they finish college should return
   to school to earn their degrees.
       "There's no question that we realize the importance of an athlete
   going back to school to finish his degree," Simmons said in a tele-
   phone interview.
       Simmons said the league had not set a definite date for a draft, but
   acknowledged that because of the league's season, (March through
   July) a winter draft was likely.
       Michigan Coach Bo Schembechler outlined the goals of the Big
   Ten resolution and said conference coaches and others, including Ala-
   bama's Bear Bryant, were in agreement.

CLERK OF COURSE:

Admission will be free. HEAT SHEETS will be
sold for $2.00 each day at the entrance to
the pool.

WARM-UPS on Thursday and Friday will be from
8:30-9:45 a.m. with the meet beginning at
10:00 a.m. Saturday's warm-ups will be from
7:30-8:45 a.m. with the meet beginning at
9:00 a.m.

FOOD will be sold in the tent on the grounds
between the pool and the tennis courts. All|
swimmers and spectators are asked to eat on
the grounds. NO FOOD OR DRINK IN THE POOL
AREA PLEASE. Your cooperation in following
this rule and also disposing of trash in the
barrels provided will be greatly appreciated.

T-SHIRTS, BAGS, HATS AND PATCHES will be sold
in the tent located at the entrance to the
pool. T-shirts - $9.00; bags - $9.50; hats -
$3.50; patches - $3.25; four piece package -
$24.50.

VIDEO CASSETTE copies of the meet or portions
thereof, are available through all three
Madison Video Station locations.

Results of events as they are swum will be
posted outside the bath house.

Awards will be medals for the first three
places and ribbons through twelfth place in
all events. Heat winner ribbons will be

given for all events during preliminaries and
in relay events through age twelve (12).

The Lost and Found is tocated in the bath
house.

The tent for swimmers is located on the grass
area between the tennis courts. AI! swimmers
are encouraged to remain in these areas to
prevent overcrowding in the pool area.

The staging area is located on the grounds
north of the pool.

RESTROOMS : Restroom facilities for swimmers and
spectators are located south of the tennis
courts. THERE WILL BE NO ADMITTANCE TO THE
POOL BUILDING EXCEPT BY MEET OFFICIALS.

It is expected that each pool ciub will be responsible for the

conduct of its swimmers. Any swimmer whose conduct is harmful to

others or to property will be asked to leave the meet.

Please observe the NO SMOKING rule in the pool area.

final team totals. Ribbons will be awarded to each relay team on the basis of

                                                                                                       Ridgewood swims to title
                                                                                                          Ridgewood swimmers won 15
                                                                                                      events, broke three city records and
                                                                                                      scored 1,322 points to outdistance sec-
                                                                                                      ond-place Monona and win the All-
                                                                                                      City Swim Meet on Saturday after-
                                                                                                      noon at the Cherokee Country Club
                                                                                                      Pool. It was Ridgewood's second con-
                                                                                                      secutive city championship.
                                                                                                         Ridgewood's Andrea Wolosz won
                                                                                                      the girls' 11-12-year-old 50-meter
                                                                                                      backstroke in a record 34.24 seconds.
                                                                                                      Wolosz also swam on the record-set-
                                                                                                      ting 200 medley and 200 freestyle
              ^                                                                                       relay teams.
                                                                                                         In boys' races, Shorewood's Bill
                                                                                                      Ragatz won the 15-17-year-old 100
                                                                                                      breaststroke and 100 butterfly. His
                                                                                                      time of 1:08.34 in the breaststroke
                                                                                                      broke his old mark of 1:08.50.
